While both Prime BTO flats and Plus resale flats share a 10-year Minimum Occupation Period (MOP) and a prohibition on whole-flat rentals, they differ in subsidy clawback (recovery) requirements: a Prime BTO flat incurs a subsidy recovery upon its first sale by the original flat buyer, whereas a Plus resale flat bought on the open market is exempt from subsidy recovery for the secondary buyer.

Here are the exact policy details based on the retrieved documents:

* **Minimum Occupation Period (MOP):** Both Prime BTO flats and Plus flats carry a 10-year MOP (Passage [1], Passage [3]).
* **Subsidy Recovery (Clawback):** 
  * *Prime BTO:* When owners of Prime flats bought from HDB sell or transfer their flat, they must return a percentage of the resale price or valuation (whichever is higher) to HDB, commensurate with the additional subsidies received (Passage [1], Passage [2], Passage [4]).
  * *Plus Resale:* If you buy a Plus flat as a resale flat on the open market, the subsidy recovery does not apply when you subsequently sell it (Passage [3]). However, original buyers of Plus BTO flats from HDB are subject to subsidy recovery upon selling or transferring their flat (Passage [1], Passage [4]).
* **Whole-Flat Rental Restrictions:** Renting out the whole flat is not allowed for both Prime and Plus flats (Passage [1], Passage [3]).

Flat owners can apply for the HDB EIP Buyback Assistance Scheme if they have made regular genuine attempts over a continuous period to sell their flat at a reasonable asking price while constrained by one or more Ethnic Integration Policy (EIP) limits [https://www.hdb.gov.sg/hdb-pulse/news/2022/more-support-for-flat-owners-constrained-by-the-ethnic-inegration-policy].

- **Marketing Period:** Flat owners must have marketed their flat for a period comparable to the time taken by most flat owners to sell their flats, which HDB considers to be presently six months [https://www.hdb.gov.sg/hdb-pulse/news/2022/more-support-for-flat-owners-constrained-by-the-ethnic-inegration-policy].
- **Reasonable Asking Price:** Flat owners must set a reasonable asking price by referencing recent transaction prices for flats within 200m and making adjustments for specific flat attributes such as storey height and orientation [https://www.hdb.gov.sg/hdb-pulse/news/2022/more-support-for-flat-owners-constrained-by-the-ethnic-inegration-policy].
- **Marketing Records:** Flat owners must keep and submit monthly records of their marketing attempts—such as online or print property listings showing asking prices and listing dates, and records of flat viewings—when seeking assistance [https://www.hdb.gov.sg/hdb-pulse/news/2022/more-support-for-flat-owners-constrained-by-the-ethnic-inegration-policy].
- **Extenuating Circumstances:** Flat owners who do not fulfill these specific criteria but face extenuating circumstances may still seek special consideration from HDB [https://www.hdb.gov.sg/hdb-pulse/news/2022/more-support-for-flat-owners-constrained-by-the-ethnic-inegration-policy]. 

This scheme applies to eligible flat owners who bought their flats directly from HDB or on the resale market, regardless of whether the flat was EIP-constrained at the time of purchase [https://www.hdb.gov.sg/hdb-pulse/news/2022/more-support-for-flat-owners-constrained-by-the-ethnic-inegration-policy].
